period_rules.week_numbering: Week N = Nth Monday-Sunday week of the calendar month, counting only weeks containing at least one attendance day. 01-02 Aug 2026 was a weekend, so Week 1 = 03-09 Aug.
period_rules.qa_week_warning: The QA export's own 'Week' column uses a DIFFERENT convention (it labels 01 Aug as Week 1 and 03-05 Aug as Week 2). NEVER filter QA on that column. Always filter QA on 'Date of Call'.
period_rules.bi_filter_warning: The BI exports arrive pre-filtered on the Salesforce sales-month, which is WIDER than the calendar month. Re-filter on Contract Create Date on ingest, or July activations leak into August.

sources.retired_note: The whole floor dials on ViciDial from 1 Sep 2026 (Nick, 2026-09-01: 'there is no longer a need for call x/call records all the agents will be on vicci now'). The upload intake refuses rows dated on/after this date and points at the ViciDial slot; earlier days still load as history corrections. Courtesy/Nesting talk time and dialler-derived Actual Shifts read ViciDial from the cutover — the shift rule itself (talk>0 -> 1) is unchanged, only where the talk comes from. NOTE the talk-time definition changes with the source: CallX billed Billable Seconds (connected leg only), ViciDial bills length_in_sec (ringing included, ~38%, per the 2026-08-13 decision) — September Courtesy talk therefore reads higher than August for the same work.

sources.grain: PRE-AGGREGATED, one row per agent for the whole period. Cannot be stacked with call_x_call.

feeds: Calls, Answered, Insurance Opt-In and dialler Sales dispositions
sources.grain: ONE ROW PER CALL, dated per call. Unlike vici_cuddle this splits across its own days, so a multi-day pull needs no apportioning and no estimate flag.
sources.join_note: 'user' carries the agent's employee code directly. NOT 'owner' - blank on 1249 of the reference pull's 2317 rows and disagreeing with 'user' on another 68. Identity still resolves through agent_roster; a code on no roster is flagged unmatched, never invented.

talk_time.caveat: length_in_sec runs from dial to hangup and therefore includes ringing. On the 2026-08-13 reference pull 32% of the seconds (17h51m of 55h27m) sit on statuses that reached no one - No Answer averages 32s, Busy 102s, Answering Machine 57s. This is the same trap call_x_call documents for 'Duration' vs 'Billable Seconds'. The engine reports the split on every upload.
talk_time.alternative: talkFrom = 'contacted' bills only rows whose status is not in no_contact_statuses.

sources.record_key_note: Unique across all 2317 rows of the reference pull. Repeats within a file are counted once; across files the fuller agent-day wins, never the sum.
sources.no_contact_note: ViciDial status CODES meaning nobody was reached. Note 'A' is Answering Machine in this export, NOT answered. These set Answered (and so AHT and Answer %), and affect talk time only when talkFrom is 'contacted'.

dispositions.opt_in: isOptIn - contains 'insurance opt' and not 'no insurance'. Verified: 'Sale Insurance Opt-In' counts, 'Sale No Insurance Opt-In' and 'VAS Sale No Insurance Opt In' do not.
dispositions.sale: isSaleDisp - all four Sale* dispositions count.

identity_resolution.principle: Employee Code is canonical. Names are display labels. Resolve every source row to an Employee Code before grouping.
resolution_order: 1. Use the source's Employee Code, after applying code_corrections.
2. Else match the dialler label against agent_roster.'Call x' (normalised).
3. Else match the person name against agent_roster.'Agent Name', then 'Sales Force' (normalised).
4. Else route to UNMAPPED and report. Never guess.
identity_resolution.normalisation: lowercase, trim, strip all non-alphanumeric characters

august_fact_table.integrity: Zero duplicates on Date + Emp Code. Assert this on every build.

columns.name: Date
columns.note: Stored as TEXT, not a date serial. Parse day-first when reading. Excel will not group this field by month/day in a pivot - that is intentional and matches the reference.

columns.name: Campaign
columns.critical: Use exactly these three tokens. The roster sheet writes 'Courtesy - Nesting'; the fact table must write 'Nesting'. The pivot page-field items are bound to these literal strings.

columns.name: Agent
columns.note: This is the pivot row label AND the VLOOKUP key used by the MTD sheets for Cancellations and QA. It must be byte-identical across the fact table, the cancellations range and the QA range.
columns.critical: Use the 'Sales Force' column, NOT 'Agent Name'. CB156 is 'Kasavani Snakarparsad' under Agent Name but 'Ashnee Kasavani Sankarparsad' under Sales Force; the tracker uses the latter, and this string is the join key for Cancellations and QA.

columns.name: Emp Code
columns.note: Canonical identity key. Not used in the pivot, but required for all joins.

columns.name: Employed Shifts
columns.rule: ALWAYS literal 1. One row exists per agent per employed day, so the MTD sum equals the agent's employed day count. Never write 2 to represent two days - write two rows.

columns.name: Actual Shifts
columns.formula: Courtesy/Nesting: 0.5 if attendance Status Code = HDCA, else 1.0 if Talk Time > 0, else 0.0. Cuddle: attendance_shift_weights[Status Code].
columns.verified: 131/136 fact rows. Residual: Mzwandile Masuku (dialled 5,125s, reference shows 0) and Surprise Lucky Cwele (0.5 with no attendance record) are manual overrides.
columns.critical: Courtesy/Nesting shifts are DIALLER-derived, not HR-derived. The attendance register disagrees with the reference tracker for 6 Courtesy agents in both directions; the talk-time rule reproduces 131/136 rows. Cuddle must use attendance because the Vici export is period-aggregated.

columns.name: Att %
columns.note: The reference omits IFERROR here. Safe because H is always 1.

columns.name: Sales Target
columns.note: Daily target. MTD target = SUM over rows, so it scales automatically with employed days.

columns.name: Sales Achieved
columns.replacement_formula: COUNT DISTINCT Case Number from bi_active WHERE Owner=Agent AND Contract Create Date = this row Date (net of cancellation)
columns.note: The reference pulled this from the external daily Variance Report. Now computed directly from the BI exports - verified exact.

columns.name: Talk Time
columns.formula: SUM(Billable Seconds) for this Emp Code on this Date, converted to a time value
columns.source: DIALLER-SIDE talk metric. Cuddle: Vici 'TALK'. Courtesy/Nesting: the daily dialler export used by the Variance Report 'Call X' sheet (NOT SUPPLIED).
columns.critical: Use Billable Seconds, NOT Duration. Duration includes ring time and overstates by ~60%.
columns.fallback: Call X Call 'Billable Seconds' is the only available Courtesy proxy but is a CARRIER measure and runs a median 4.8% high (range 1.001x to 1.306x). Use it only as an interim estimate and flag it.

columns.name: GWP Achieved

row_inclusion_rule.rule: One row per roster agent per dialing day. Driven by the ROSTER, not attendance. Agents with no attendance record still get rows (the 3 Nesting agents have none). Agents with zero sales and zero talk still get rows - their zeros are required for the % Of Agents on Target denominator.
row_inclusion_rule.dialing_days: Distinct dates in the attendance register within the period.

derived_column_formulas._comment: The seven ratio/derived columns that must ALWAYS be formulas, never pasted numbers. Each has an explicit numerator and denominator and a zero-denominator result of 0.
derived_column_formulas._grand_total_rule: On the Grand Total row every one of these is recomputed from the SUMMED numerator and denominator (e.g. =IFERROR((P{gt}/I{gt}),0)). Never average the agent-row percentages. Averaging Ave GWP across agents gives a different and wrong answer to total GWP / total sales.

qa_rules.period_filter: Date of Assessment BETWEEN mtd_start AND mtd_end (fallback: Submitted At, then Date of Call). NOT the file's own Week column. CHANGED 2026-08-26 by Nick, superseding the v6.0 Date-of-Call rule: QA is credited to the day the QA team did the work. Assessments lag calls by 1-4 days, so filing on call date made every fresh upload look like it had not landed ('there is data until the 25th'). The reference workbook's QA pivot was built on Date of Call, so per-period QA figures legitimately diverge from it from this date forward.
qa_rules.score_parsing: Strip '%', cast to float, divide by 100. Values carry one decimal place (e.g. '93.9%'). Never aggregate as text.

headline_metric.name: QA
headline_metric.verified: 26/44 agents exact against the reference pivot; no filter variant scored higher.
headline_metric.no_data_value: "No QA %" (text). AVERAGE() ignores it, so agents with no evaluation are excluded from the denominator rather than counted as zero.

critical_fail_equivalence.finding: Score % = 0% <=> Escalation Decision = 'Critical Fail'. Perfect correspondence, 24/24 in the reference period.
critical_fail_equivalence.implication: Zero scores are real outcomes, not missing data. Never treat 0% as null and never exclude it from the average - doing so inflates every affected agent's score.

rejected_filters._comment: Tested against the reference QA pivot; exact-agent match shown. Unfiltered scores 26/44 and wins.

campaign_normalisation._note: QA covers Tracker (Vehicle Tracking) agents outside VAS scope. Retained in the headline average to match the reference, but flagged - see OI-13.

workflow_metrics.name: QA Evaluations
workflow_metrics.note: Denominator for every QA rate. An agent with one evaluation and one critical fail shows 100% - always read the rate alongside the volume.

workflow_metrics.name: Pass %
workflow_metrics.note: Derived rather than counted so the three outcomes always sum to 100%.

workflow_metrics.name: P1 Priority
workflow_metrics.note: Priority is null on passes; P1/P2/P3 populate only on Critical Fail or Coaching.

workflow_metrics.name: Disputes
workflow_metrics.note: Dispute Status runs Pending / Upheld / Rejected. An UPHELD dispute means the recorded score was wrong, so the period's QA is provisional.

workflow_metrics.name: QA Open
workflow_metrics.note: Covers Pending TL Action, Awaiting QA Close, TL Stage 1 Complete. Open items can still change score or outcome.

workflow_metrics.name: Callback Required
workflow_metrics.note: Operational follow-up, not a scoring metric.

common_configuration.exclusion_rationale: Ratio columns are NEVER summed or averaged in the pivot. They are recomputed downstream in the MTD sheets from the summed numerator and denominator. This is what prevents averaging-of-averages error.

lookup_ranges_not_pivots.warning: These three ranges sit on the 'Pivot Table' sheet and LOOK like pivots, but the workbook contains only two pivotTable parts. They are pasted value ranges maintained outside the workbook. The engine must generate them as sorted lookup tables.

ranges.filter: Contract Create Date BETWEEN mtd_start AND mtd_end

Date of Call BETWEEN week_start AND week_end

mtd_sheet_construction.header_whitespace_note: Several headers carry a trailing space in the reference ('Employed Shifts ', 'Att % ') and column J carries a LEADING space (' % of Sales Target '). Reproduce exactly if downstream consumers match on header text.

ratio_columns.rule: RECOMPUTE from the summed numerator and denominator. NEVER average the agent-row percentages.

processing_pipeline.name: INGEST
processing_pipeline.action: Load all sources. Assert each file's period header falls in the expected window. Record row counts.

processing_pipeline.name: CLEAN
processing_pipeline.action: Strip footer rows, trim headers, cast dates, parse Score % and durations, normalise campaign vocabulary.

processing_pipeline.name: RESOLVE IDENTITY
processing_pipeline.action: Map every row to an Employee Code. Route failures to UNMAPPED.

processing_pipeline.name: FILTER PERIOD
processing_pipeline.action: Apply mtd_start/mtd_end to each source on its designated date field.

processing_pipeline.name: DEDUPLICATE
processing_pipeline.action: Apply each source's dedup_key. Record counts removed.

processing_pipeline.name: BUILD FACT TABLE
processing_pipeline.action: Append one row per agent per day to 'August'. Assert uniqueness on Date+Emp Code.

processing_pipeline.name: EXTEND CACHE
processing_pipeline.action: Update the pivot cache ref to August!A1:T{lastrow}, then refresh both pivots once.

processing_pipeline.name: BUILD LOOKUP RANGES
processing_pipeline.action: Regenerate N:O, U:V and AA:AB. Preserve Q:S commentary.

processing_pipeline.name: BUILD QA METRICS
processing_pipeline.action: Group filtered evaluations by Employee Code and compute the nine workflow metrics alongside the headline average.

processing_pipeline.name: RENDER SHEETS
processing_pipeline.action: Write MTD, WTD and TL sheets with live formulas, not pasted values.

processing_pipeline.name: REPORT
processing_pipeline.action: Emit the validation summary alongside the workbook.

processing_pipeline.name: RECALCULATE
processing_pipeline.action: Recalculate the saved workbook and re-save so every formula carries a cached result. MANDATORY - without it all formula cells display blank in previewers, on mobile, and in any tool that does not evaluate formulas. Headless LibreOffice round-trip is sufficient.

SUM(August[Sales Achieved]) == COUNT DISTINCT (agent, date, Case Number) tuples in the filtered BI union

SUM(August[Employed Shifts]) == COUNT of filtered attendance rows

Grand-total ratio cells are formulas referencing the total row, not averages of the agent rows
The N:O cancellations range lists every agent present in the fact table

UNMAPPED bucket is empty; if not, list every unmapped record

validation_checks.check: Pivot cache ref covers the full August used range
validation_checks.rationale: A stale ref silently drops the newest day from every downstream figure.

validation_checks.check: Every formula cell has a cached value after the recalculation step
validation_checks.rationale: Formulas written by a library carry no cached result. Without recalculation the report looks like it has missing data even though the formulas are correct.

validation_checks.rationale: An upheld dispute retrospectively changes a score, making the period's QA provisional.

money_model_unit.rule: Sales Achieved = COUNT DISTINCT Case Number per agent per Contract Create Date over bi_active only (NET of cancellation). GWP = SUM(Charge Amount) within the case, rounded per case, x1.15.
money_model_unit.uncased_rows: No Case Number = recurring feature line (Positions/Trips/Panic/Geoloc, no Case Type). Pooled per agent-day as ~uncased: counted in GWP, never a sale.
money_model_unit.supersedes: The former COUNT DISTINCT Account Number over UNION(bi_active, bi_inactive).
money_model_unit.net_of_cancellation_note: TRUE since 2026-08-18 (owner directive). Sales count what is still active. The reference workbook counts gross and is knowingly superseded; the divergence is pinned per agent in verify-mtd-values.
money_model_unit.gwp_display_note: Owner directive 2026-08-18: ex-VAT is the agent comms basis, so GWP Achieved / Ave GWP / GWP Target display ex-VAT on every VAS page (Enoch Aug = R11,115, the source pivot Sum of Charge Amount). The VAT-inclusive figure is kept internally (gwpIncl) and VAT remains in exactly one reporting place: the Variance Report DV02, whose comparison target — the agent-logged board — is written VAT-inclusive.
